notes:
Overview: Spectra CI Labs builds an IDE copilot focused on developer workflows that require code execution: running unit/integration tests, linters, and surfacing build logs inline in the editor. They want function-calling tooling so the agent can 'run tests' and return structured results + log streaming.

Primary requirements (from discovery):
- Sandboxed execution: ephemeral containers + strict network egress controls, must support air-gapped on-prem installs for regulated customers.
- Low-latency streaming for completions in IDE (goal: interactive feel, token latency <100ms, ideally sub-50ms for local/private models).
- Model/version pinning: need to pin model revisions for reproducibility across releases and A/B test new model builds.
- Tool/function calling: run tests, run linters, collect stdout/stderr and build artifacts; agent should return structured pass/fail + trace links.
- Audit and retention: immutable audit logs, per-team retention policies for logs, ability to ship logs to customer S3 or internal ELK.

Technical targets and constraints: 
- Throughput: expect 200 concurrent active developers at peak day-of-week; typical agent interactions are short but frequent (50-200 reqs/min sustained across teams).
- Latency SLOs: median generation latency <120ms; 95th <300ms for small completions used for token-by-token streaming in editor.
- Preferred models: open quantized families (Llama-3/Alpaca-style) for on-prem; also want capability to fall back to hosted curated models for spikes.
- Cost sensitivity: high — early stage monetization; looking for Optimize suggestions (batching, KV cache for prefix code, quantization profiles) to drive unit-token cost down.

Recent timeline & activities: 
- 2025-11-05: Intro call (Maya) — demo of copilot; customer demo showed test-run flow prototype (agent calls test_run(tool_id, params)).
- 2025-12-08: Security questionnaire sent; Spectra provided initial network constraints doc.
- 2026-01-12: Follow-up technical deep dive (Lena) — discussed container sandboxing approach, required HSM for signing test artifacts, audit log formats. Fireflies: ff-20260108-4532.
- 2026-02-20: Request for POC template and sample harness (w/ sample repos). Gmail thread: thread-Gm-20260220-poc-logs.
- 2026-03-03: Pricing deck shared; Drive: drive://spectraci/Redwood_POC_Playbook.pdf.
- 2026-03-10: Internal sizing call — decided to evaluate Dedicated vs Private POC.

What Spectra is looking for from Redwood: 
- A sandboxed function-calling model that can spawn ephemeral containers (or call an execution layer) and stream logs back to the editor without exposing customer secrets.
- Model pinning + rollout controls (canary) so product team can A/B new model weights when changing test-understanding behavior.
- Cost/perf recommendations: quantization suggestions and batching policy for short interactive completions.
- Clear audit trail and retention controls for execution logs for regulated customers.

Quotes / call snippets: 
- "We need the agent to actually run tests, not just guess results — show me the log and the failing assertion." — Lead Eng (demo).
- "Air-gapped customers will be deal-breakers unless we have a hardened on-prem package and installer." — CTO.

Open questions / unknowns for POC: 
- Execution surface: Redwood to propose options for secure tool-calls (sidecar exec vs RPC to tenant-managed runner).
- How to attach signed artifacts to audit log (HSM vs KMS flow).
- Performance baseline for streaming with quantized models on Dedicated nodes.

Next steps (short): 
- Redwood to provide Dedicated POC spec + infra cost estimate (Lena).
- Share on-prem installer checklist and sandbox network diagram by 2026-03-17.
- Schedule security review with Spectra infra sec and legal (owner: Maya).

Sales notes / strategy: 
- Upside: enterprise customers in finance and healthcare may require air-gapped installs — close >50% of pipeline if on-prem POC is successful.
- Pricing sensitivity — expect negotiation on commit level; aim for 12mo reserved capacity.
- Bring in Solutions Architect early (for sandbox design) and Regulatory SME for ISO/SOC artifacts.
